# Binary size baselines, in bytes, per target triple.
#
# Checked by .github/scripts/check-binary-size.sh against the `dist` profile
# build. Growth beyond the tolerance (default 5%) fails the build.
#
# These are USER-VISIBLE numbers: omni ships as a single self-contained
# binary, so this is what people download. Before this gate existed the
# binary had reached 28 MB with no [profile.release] section at all.
#
# To change a baseline deliberately:
#   UPDATE_BASELINE=1 .github/scripts/check-binary-size.sh <binary> <target>
# and include the result in the pull request so it gets reviewed.
#
# Format: "<target-triple>\t<bytes>"
#
# Targets not listed here are reported but do not fail, so adding a new
# target does not break the build before its baseline is recorded.
#
# The four shipped targets below were recorded from a green CI run. They are
# the numbers users actually download.
aarch64-unknown-linux-musl	15896240
x86_64-unknown-linux-musl	19902536
aarch64-apple-darwin	15850432
x86_64-apple-darwin	18319240

# Not built by CI -- a local glibc host build, kept only as a reference for
# iterating locally. Refresh it by hand; nothing verifies it.
aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu	16551848

# Note: the x86_64 binaries are ~3 MB larger than their aarch64 equivalents
# (18.98 vs 15.16 MB on musl). blake3 is a likely contributor -- on x86_64 it
# compiles several SIMD variants into the binary
# (blake3_avx512_assembly *and* blake3_sse2_sse41_avx2_assembly) where
# aarch64 gets a single blake3_neon. Worth investigating as a size lead; see
# PLAN/01-binary-size.md.
